records.rationale: A permissive `may`: it authorizes an implementation to inject the declared secrets as environment variables and requires nothing. A clause that forbids no behavior admits no failing observation, so there is no outcome an assertion could pin.

The key-naming rule is an authoring recommendation (`should` be valid POSIX environment-variable names) on the author's document. deacon neither validates secret names against that grammar nor changes behavior when one is invalid, exactly as it declines JSON-Schema pattern validation elsewhere, so the recommendation has no separately-observable consumer consequence; the `secrets` object's shape is claimed by bhv-secrets-dotenv-superset.

A negative requirement: a declared secret must not become a precondition of container creation. deacon models `secrets` as descriptive metadata only (config.rs `secrets: Option<HashMap<String, SecretMetadata>>`, never consulted on the creation path), so no configuration exists in which creation could be gated on one; the property holds by construction of the model rather than as an outcome any channel discriminates.
